attacks.detail: 19 git-unsafe affixes, format-like affixes, 9 hostile branch names, 30 regex patterns incl. very long and nested. Findings are seeds 1 to 4.

seeds.title: preflight crashes with a traceback on a non-string rule pattern
seeds.detail: A forge rule whose pattern is a list, null, number or object makes _raw_result raise TypeError (startswith/endswith/in) or re.compile raise TypeError for regex. preflight exits 1 with a Python traceback on stderr and no JSON on stdout. The code is S-015's, not in the S-016 diff; derive() itself returns None for these. See TC-cli-6.

seeds.title: preflight hangs on a catastrophic regex rule
seeds.detail: Rule regex (((((((((((((((((((((a*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*)*b evaluated on sdlc/state-20261010120000 does not finish in 10 s; preflight hit the 30 s runner timeout. Short samples like sdlc/S-001 return at once. Code is in S-015's _raw_result (re.search on a forge-supplied pattern). See logs/cli-0-probes.txt.

seeds.title: rename suggestion puts the branch name unquoted into a shell line
seeds.detail: suggest() writes git branch -m <name> <new-name> with the raw name. For --branch '$(id)' or a backtick name, pasting the line runs the command. A name with a quote, space or backslash is read back wrong by sh. A name with a newline splits the suggestion into three lines. Names are user supplied, so the risk is low. See VS-5b lines in logs/cli-0-transcripts.txt.

seeds.title: _regex_literal builds an unbounded string for nested counted repeats
seeds.detail: _shortest multiplies repeat counts as strings. Pattern ((a{1000}){1000}){1000} (25 characters) took 19 s and 5.9 GB peak RSS in _regex_literal; ((a{1000}){1000}){100} took 1.9 s and 637 MB. A larger count can exhaust memory. A forge admin supplies the pattern. A cap on the built length would remove the risk. See logs/cli-0-probes.txt.
